body:
Cloudflare's free-plan proxy can't see raw TCP mail traffic at all (mail DNS record stays unproxied for delivery to work), so real geo-blocking had to happen at the host firewall. Flagged and got confirmation on a real risk before implementing: geo-blocking SMTP (25) by source IP could silently drop legitimate inbound mail since big providers don't route by sender geography. Scoped to the real human-login surfaces only (443 webmail, 993 IMAPS, 8080 admin panel). Built a UFW-hooked ipset (ipdeny.com CIDR data, US+MX+CA, ~80k entries, no API key needed), persisted across reboot, weekly auto-refresh. Verified live on the real server: rule active, correctly includes/excludes real test IPs, this session's own US connections still work end to end. Commit b827139.

⚓ ☃
title: Mail server geo-restricted to US/MX/CA for webmail/IMAPS/admin -- SMTP left open, verified live
